title: 2022_PMC8993071_COVID-19_vaccination_in_5-11_years_old_children_Drivers_of_vacci
ehr_evidence: four focus group discussions were conducted with 28 vaccine-hesitant parents on November 8 and 9, 2021, three weeks after the submission of Pfizer-BioNTech’ application to Health Canada for approval of its pediatric formulation of its COVID-19 vaccine.
summary: Qualitative study exploring drivers of COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy among parents of 5-11 year old children in Quebec using focus group discussions.
key_findings: Out of 28 participants, seven intended to vaccinate their child(ren) while the remaining were unsure or unwilling.
Parents perceived vaccination as unnecessary due to low child risk and were concerned about side effects and political pressure.
Focus group findings may not be representative of most parents due to recruitment of vaccine-hesitant participants.
captured_features: perceptions of vaccine safety and necessity
population: parents of 5-11 year old children in Quebec, Canada
limitations: recruited only vaccine-hesitant parents, limiting representativeness
